protocol_overview.type: Source-synchronous low-power mobile memory bus. Controller-driven quarter-speed differential clock (CK) + 7-bit double-data-rate command/address (CA) bus + chip select (CS), with a separately-enabled full-speed differential Write Clock (WCK) and DRAM-driven Read Strobe (RDQS) framing the bidirectional double-data-rate DQ data bus.
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex on DQ (read or write, not both simultaneously); CK / CA / CS / WCK are controller → SDRAM; RDQS is SDRAM → controller during reads

write_clock: WCK_c (differential, full-speed, 4x CK; enabled only when a transfer is imminent)
chip_select: CS (active-high; bounds low-power-mode duration; replaces the CKE pin of LPDDR4)
command_address: CA[6:0] (7-bit, double-data-rate; commands span rising + falling CK edges)
data: DQ[15:0] per channel (two x8 byte groups)
data_mask_dbi: DMI (Data Mask / Data Bus Inversion, per byte group)

protocol_overview.ddr_signaling: Data (DQ) is sampled on both edges of WCK (write) / RDQS (read) — double data rate at the full WCK rate. Command/address (CA[6:0]) is also double-data-rate but referenced to the quarter-speed CK, so a command consumes two CA transfers (one on the rising and one on the falling CK edge).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Bus master. Drives CK/CK_c (quarter speed), CA[6:0], CS, RESET_n. Drives WCK during writes (and to pre-synchronize for reads). Sources DQ + DMI during write; sinks DQ during read while the DRAM drives RDQS. Implements WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR), refresh (all-bank/per-bank), DVFS, link-ECC encode/decode, and per-bank state tracking.
protocol_overview.sdram_role: Bus slave. Decodes the 7-bit DDR CA bus into commands per the LPDDR5 command encoding table. Locks its internal WCK to CK during the WCK2CK synchronization window before a transfer. Drives DQ + RDQS during read; sinks DQ + DMI during write. Generates internal refresh; honours bank-group timing; supports deep sleep and CA-bus-bounded power-down (no CKE).

functional_requirements.text: The LPDDR5 SDRAM shall use a quarter-speed differential master clock CK_t/CK_c as the command/address timing reference, and a separate full-speed differential Write Clock WCK_t/WCK_c (running at 4x the CK rate) that is enabled only when a data transfer is imminent.
During reads the LPDDR5 SDRAM shall drive a full-speed differential Read Strobe RDQS_t/RDQS_c edge-aligned with the read data; RDQS is enabled only when a read is in progress.

Before a high-speed read or write, the controller shall issue a WCK2CK synchronization sequence (WS_FS free-start, WS_RD read-optimized, or WS_WR write-optimized), carried by the CAS command, so the DRAM can lock its internal WCK phase to CK; WS_FS starts the clock immediately and may be followed by multiple reads/writes, while WS_RD/WS_WR optimize timing for an immediately following read/write.
Command/address shall be transferred on a 7-bit CA bus (CA[6:0]) at double data rate; a command occupies two CA transfers (rising CK edge then falling CK edge) per the LPDDR5 command encoding table.
LPDDR5 shall NOT use a Clock Enable (CKE) pin. Low-power mode shall be entered by a command over the CA bus and shall last until the chip select (CS) signal next goes high.

LPDDR5 SDRAM shall provide 16 banks, organizable as four DDR4-style bank groups of four banks each (bank-group mode), 16 flat banks (16B mode), or 8 banks (8B mode) per density; bank/bank-group is selected by BA / BG address fields on the CA bus.

LPDDR5 SDRAM shall implement a 16n prefetch architecture; unlike earlier generation transitions the prefetch is not doubled relative to LPDDR4 and remains 16n. Default burst length shall be 16 (BL16); a double-length burst of 32 (BL32) is also supported.
The LPDDR5 interface shall support data transfer rates up to 6400 Mbit/s per pin (WCK at 3200 MHz, CK at 800 MHz). LPDDR5X (JESD209-5B/5X) shall extend the rate up to 8533 Mbit/s.
The DQ/IO supply VDDQ shall be reduced to 0.5 V to lower IO power; core supplies VDD1 and VDD2H/VDD2L shall be provided, with DVFSC selecting VDD2H or VDD2L for dynamic core voltage scaling.

LPDDR5 shall support Read Link ECC and Write Link ECC (16-bit link ECC) providing single-bit error correction on the data carried across the bus; Data Bus Inversion (DBI) on the DMI lines shall be supported to minimize the number of bits driven during transfers.
LPDDR5 SDRAM shall accept all-bank refresh (REFab) and per-bank refresh (REFpb, round-robin bank address) commands; refresh interval shall honour tREFI (per temperature range) and tRFCab / tRFCpb.

LPDDR5 shall support power-saving features including deep sleep mode (DSM), dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS / DVFSC), Data-Copy and Write-X (all-zero / all-one) commands to reduce data transfer, and partial-array / per-bank refresh granularity.
The LPDDR5 receiver shall support Decision Feedback Equalization (DFE) and tx/rx equalization (added in JESD209-5B) to maintain signal integrity at 6400+ Mbit/s.
LPDDR5 SDRAM may implement a two-deck architecture (deck mode) that splits the device into two decks for finer power and access granularity.

As in LPDDR4, reading data shall require multiple commands: two Activate commands (Activate-1, Activate-2) to select a row, followed by a CAS (column address select) command and then the Read or Write command; in LPDDR5 the CAS command comes BEFORE the read/write and primarily prepares the DRAM to synchronize with the imminent WCK clock (it does not by itself select a column).

The CAS command shall also specify the Write-X (WRX) option: when set, writes do not transfer data on the bus but rather fill the burst with all-zeros or all-ones under control of the WXS (write-X select) bit, saving the same amount of time as a normal write while saving power.
RESET_n shall be an active-low reset input that returns the device to its reset state; mode registers are volatile and must be re-programmed after reset / power-up.

configurations.name: Bank-group mode (BG mode)
configurations.description: 16 banks arranged as four bank groups of four banks; bank-group timing (tCCD_L / tRRD_L between same-group accesses) applies.

configurations.name: 8-bank mode (8B)
configurations.description: 8 banks for selected densities / lower-power configurations.

configurations.name: WCK2CK sync — Free-Start (WS_FS)
configurations.description: Starts the WCK clock immediately; may be followed by multiple reads/writes accessing multiple banks.

configurations.name: WCK2CK sync — Read-optimized (WS_RD)
configurations.description: Optimizes WCK timing for an immediately following read command.

configurations.name: WCK2CK sync — Write-optimized (WS_WR)
configurations.description: Optimizes WCK timing for an immediately following write command.

configurations.name: Burst length 32 (BL32)
configurations.description: Double-length 32-beat burst; reads may specify a starting position within the 32-word-aligned burst using the C0 and B3 column bits.

configurations.name: Write-X (WRX, all-zero / all-one)
configurations.description: Burst filled with all-zeros or all-ones (per WXS bit) without transferring data — saves IO power.

configurations.name: DVFSC (Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling Core)
configurations.description: Selects VDD2H or VDD2L to scale core voltage with operating frequency.

configurations.name: Deep Sleep Mode (DSM)
configurations.description: Lowest standby power; entered via CA-bus command (Deep Sleep Enable bit); full re-init / exit sequence required to leave.

configurations.name: All-bank refresh (REFab)
configurations.description: Refreshes all banks; DRAM blocked during tRFCab.

configurations.name: Per-bank refresh (REFpb)
configurations.description: Refreshes one bank per command in round-robin bank order; allows access to other banks during tRFCpb.

error_response_conditions: Link-ECC uncorrectable error (more than one bit flipped within an ECC word on the wire) — LPDDR5 link ECC is single-bit correcting; a multi-bit error is not corrected and may be flagged depending on configuration.
WCK2CK synchronization not performed before a high-speed read/write — the DRAM's internal WCK phase is not locked to CK and read/write data timing is undefined.
Refresh interval missed (more than the allowed window between REF commands) — cell content may be lost; the DRAM does not flag the error at the protocol level.
CA-bus parity / illegal command in current state — behaviour is undefined; the controller must obey the LPDDR5 state diagram and command encoding.
Mode Register Set issued without all banks idle and timing satisfied — result is undefined.
Deep-sleep exit without the required re-initialization sequence — DRAM state is undefined; full power-up init is required.
compliance_requirements: Power-up + initialization sequence (RESET_n assertion, supply ramp ordering for VDD1 / VDD2H / VDD2L / VDDQ, CK start, mode-register programming, ZQ calibration, WCK2CK initial synchronization) must complete before normal operation.
WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS / WS_RD / WS_WR via CAS) shall be performed to lock the internal WCK to CK before any high-speed read or write.
Refresh: average interval ≤ tREFI per temperature range; REFab and REFpb timing (tRFCab / tRFCpb) shall be honoured; per-bank refresh follows round-robin bank order.
Bank-group timing (tCCD_L / tRRD_L) shall be honoured between accesses to the same bank group in BG mode; tCCD_S / tRRD_S between different bank groups.
VDDQ shall be regulated to 0.5 V; core supplies VDD1 / VDD2H / VDD2L per the operating point; DVFSC transitions shall follow the defined voltage/frequency change procedure.
Low-power-mode entry shall be issued as a CA-bus command (no CKE pin) and shall last until CS next goes high.
Link ECC (Read/Write) and DBI shall be configured consistently between controller and DRAM; mismatched configuration corrupts data silently.
Deep sleep entry/exit, DVFS, and frequency change shall follow the defined sequences; clock frequency change is only allowed in the defined low-power / sync windows.
